# A remote Store's load params do not reach the server intact

## Context

`Store#load` builds its read params (`page`, `pageSize`, `filters` from `exportFilters()` when `remoteFilter`, `sorters` from `exportSorters()` when `remoteSort`, and an optional one-off `url`) and passes them through `Pipeline#read` to the connection's `read(params)` (`src/data/Store.mjs:1208–1286`). Neither HTTP connection sends them in a form a server can use. Found while reading the remote paging path for a server-backed grid in a package built on the engine.

Reproducer: Node, the real `Store#load` path with `XMLHttpRequest` and `fetch` stubbed to capture the request, engine `dev` `7698a7ac5b` (the anchors below are at that commit). The store has `pageSize: 50`, `remoteFilter` and `remoteSort`, one filter and one sorter.

```
Xhr (the default pipeline a `url` config builds):
GET /api/rows?page=1&pageSize=50&filters=%5Bobject+Object%5D&sorters=%5Bobject+Object%5D
Xhr, load({url: '/api/other'}) on the same store:
GET /api/rows?page=1&pageSize=50&filters=%5Bobject+Object%5D&sorters=%5Bobject+Object%5D&url=%2Fapi%2Fother
Fetch connection:
GET /api/rows
```

## The Problem

- With `remoteSort` or `remoteFilter`, the server receives `[object Object]` for the sorter and filter lists, so it can neither sort nor filter.
- Over the Fetch connection the server receives no params at all: no page, no page size.
- A one-off `load({url})` on a store that already has a connection requests the old URL and sends the new one as a `url` query param.

The one consumer in this repository that sets both flags, `examples/toolbar/paging/store/Users.mjs`, loads through `api` (the remote-method path), so CI never sends them over an HTTP connection.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: `remoteFilter`: "True to let the backend handle the filtering." (`src/data/Store.mjs:235`). `remoteSort`: "True to let the backend handle the sorting." (`:241`). `#loadRecords`: "params.url can override pipeline/connection url" (`:1273`).

- A `url` config builds a pipeline on the Xhr connection (`Store.mjs:580`). `Xhr#read(params)` (`src/data/connection/Xhr.mjs:45`) reaches `appendParams()`, which builds `new URLSearchParams(params)` (`:63–64`, called at `:219`). `URLSearchParams` stringifies an array of objects as `[object Object]`.
- `Fetch#read(params)` calls `get(this.url, params)` (`src/data/connection/Fetch.mjs:32`), so `request()` takes the params as its request config (`headers`, `method`, `responseType`) and overwrites their `url` with the connection's (`:114–129`). Nothing reaches the query.
- #20489 taught `appendParams()` to compose into a URL that already has a query or a fragment; its Out of Scope records that Fetch composes no params. Request interceptors (#9553) reshape a read's params and return `{...params, headers}`, which #20472 sends as Fetch request headers.

## The Fix

- Move `appendParams()` to `Neo.data.connection.Base`, keeping #20489's composition rules, and encode each value: strings, numbers and booleans as they are, arrays and plain objects as JSON (`sorters=[{"property":"score","direction":"DESC"}]`, URL-encoded), `undefined` and `null` left out.
- `Xhr#read` and `Fetch#read` both GET their URL with the params composed by it. Two read params are request config, not query: `url` replaces the connection's URL for that request, and `headers` are request headers over `defaultHeaders`, the shape request interceptors return.
- `Fetch#read` stops treating any other read param as request config.

| `Neo.data.connection.Xhr#read(params)` | `Store.mjs:1208–1286` | `params.url` sets the request URL, `params.headers` are request headers, the other params compose into its query | none | JSDoc | unit |
| `Neo.data.connection.Fetch#read(params)` | `Store.mjs:1208–1286`; #20472 | GET with the params composed into the query; `params.url` sets the request URL, `params.headers` are request headers | request options from the connection | JSDoc | unit, component |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `remoteSort` + `remoteFilter` store on the `url` default pipeline sends `sorters` and `filters` that `JSON.parse` turns back into its `exportSorters()` and `exportFilters()` (unit, stubbed `XMLHttpRequest`).
- [ ] The same store on a Fetch connection sends `page`, `pageSize`, `sorters` and `filters` in its query (unit, stubbed `fetch`).
- [ ] `load({url})` on a store that has a connection requests that URL, with no `url` query param, on both connections (unit).
- [ ] #20489's composition cases still pass: an existing query, a trailing `&`, a fragment, a relative URL.
- [ ] Each new spec fails on `dev` before the fix.

## Out of Scope

- A request body for reads, and any paging protocol beyond these params.
- The `Stream`, `WebSocket` and `Rpc` connections.
- Request interceptors (#9553).

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-11-15T01:46:35Z

**Follow-up to the handover above: PR #20984's red is `dev`'s, not this change's.**

- **On `dev` without this PR:** `dev`'s own push run at `4f6f46b2d8` (run 43658119008, shard 13/14) printed the same error inside `DockReloadActionNL`; it passed only because the error landed after the spec's worker-error check. The spec also failed `dev` pushes at `3c9ef1039f`, `d6e427e7a7` and `6f1f8b2df9`. Its onset in CI history is #20961 (`3c9ef1039f`); none in 8 runs before it, 12 of 24 since.
- **Reproduced under CPU throttling,** on both heads alike: at 4× it failed 2 of 5 on each; at 6× 4 of 5 on `dev`'s tip and 3 of 5 on this PR's head.
- **Mechanism:** `HeaderActions#commitRecreateCandidate` removes the pane with `removeAt(index + 1, false)` (`src/dashboard/dock/.../HeaderActions.mjs:732`), which clears `parentId`, then destroys it (`:736`) with no parent, so the unlink in `Abstract#destroy` never runs. The main tabs' body container keeps `{componentId: 'neo-dock-pane-2'}` in its stored vnode, and a workspace render already in flight lands a few ms later and throws in `createMap` (`VdomLifecycle.mjs:1293` → `VNode.mjs:241`).
- **Smallest fix, measured as a live patch at 6×** (0 of 20 failed against 13 of 15 unpatched): right after the destroy, unlink the dead reference from the container's vnode, as `Abstract#destroy` does for a parented pane (`VNodeUtil.unlinkRetiredReferences(container.vnode, {[id]: vnode})`). It needs its own dock bug ticket with a red-first regression; prior art for this error: #18297, #20783, #20564.

This PR then needs only a re-run of its shard. Seen beside it, not yet checked: a `StoreUpdateRowsNL` red on `dev`'s shard 5.
